response.title: Visiting Christian Quarter
response.summary: The Christian Quarter occupies the north-western Old City and is centred on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, alongside monasteries, hospices, schools, homes and markets.
response.narrative:
The Christian Quarter occupies the north-western Old City and is centred on the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, alongside monasteries, hospices, schools, homes and markets.

Things to look for:
- Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
- Latin Patriarchate.
- Greek Orthodox Patriarchate.
- Souq al-Bazaar.

Byzantine era (4th century CE): The first Church of the Holy Sepulchre complex was built under Emperor Constantine.
Crusader era (12th century CE): The church was substantially rebuilt into much of the form visible today.
Ottoman era (1517-1917 CE): Christian institutions and the commercial streets around them continued under regulated communal arrangements.
uncertainty_notes: Gaps the AI must not fill: miraculous claims, exact congregation numbers and unreviewed biographies.
